item.title: Major turnout at 50th anniversary ceremony of Castleblayney bombing
item.description: A well-attended wreath-laying ceremony has taken place to mark 50 years since the Castleblayney bombing. A no-warning car bomb exploded outside the Three Star Inn on Main Street at 8:20pm on the 7th of March 1976, with 56-year-old man, Patrick 'Packie' Mone, killed in the blast. A review was launched into the incident in March 2020, and families who lost loved ones in attacks related to the Glenanne Gang are awaiting the publication of Operation Denton. item.title: Sligo crush Cavan in hurling league
item.description: Cavan fell to a heavy defeat in division four this afternoon, as Sligo put eight goals past them. Sligo scoring a 8-19 to 12-point win at the Enniscrone Kilglass GAA grounds. Gerard O’Kelly Lynch opened the scoring with a goal for Sligo after a minute of play. Advertisement Andrew Kilcullen, Conor Hanniffy and Thomas Cawley all found the back of the Cavan net in the first-half. item.description: A 36-year-old man has appeared before a special sitting of Trim District Court this evening charged in relation to the seizure of €281,000 worth of cannabis. Lithuanian national Justas Sapransaukas of no fixed abode appeared before Judge Raymond Finnegan over a number of a charges that alleges he was in possession of the drugs. item.title: Government-chartered flight from Oman arrives in Dublin
item.description: A government chartered bringing Irish citizens out of the Middle East has touched down at Dublin Airport this morning. The aircraft left Muscat in Oman yesterday afternoon and arrived shortly before five am, after a delay during a stopover in Cairo, with 200 people on board. Foreign Affairs Minister Helen McEntee says 15 hundred people have returned on commercial flights in recent days, and is urging Irish citizens in the Middle East to register their presence. item.title: Local councillor calls for 'robust approach' to repair potholes
item.description: A local councillor has called for Monaghan County Council to adopt a more "robust approach" when it comes to repairing potholes. Cllr Richard Truell has requested that Monaghan County Council's roads department as part of the 2626 roadworks programme undertake a review of current pothole repair practices. item.title: Local biodiversity projects set to benefit from new funding
item.description: Biodiversity conservation projects in Cavan and Monaghan are set to benefit from funding. €134, 844 has been announced to support biodiversity projects in Cavan and Monaghan. Nationally, the announcement provides €1.1 million in funding for 53 community projects through the Peatlands and Natura Community Engagement Scheme 2026. item.title: Lidl National Football League round-up
item.description: Carlow maintained their perfect run in Division 4 of the Lidl National Football League when they chalked up their seventh win of the campaign and in the process inflicted a first defeat of the season on Leitrim. Carlow trailed by 0-7 to 0-1 at the break but then took over after the restart and ran out 2-7 to 0-11 winners.
